::: {.why}
A permutation test is the cleanest null available for a trading rule, and it is only as good as the choice of what gets permuted, which is where most implementations go wrong.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Name three distinct permutation schemes for a strategy test and say which alternative hypothesis each one tests against.
- Run one and report the p-value of your own signal against it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Enumerate the schemes and what each preserves: permute the signal while keeping returns fixed, permute returns while keeping the signal fixed, permute the mapping between signal and forward return within time blocks, and circularly shift the signal. Write down for each what structure survives the permutation and therefore what the test is powered against.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the block-preserving version and run it: 5,000 permutations of your signal against the same return series, reporting the p-value of the observed Sharpe. Then run a signal you know is worthless as a control and confirm the p-value distribution is roughly uniform.
:::
:::
